_comment: Canonical matrix. Four harnesses, three tiers, and one answer per harness for every capability row. scripts/render_adapters.py refuses to render an incoherent matrix and regenerates every adapter from this file, so this is the only place a routing or capability fact is stated.

explore.reason: a read-only scout with the same file:line return convention ships with the harness

planner.native: the built-in Plan agent, and plan mode
planner.reason: plan mode already produces a read-only plan and holds it at an approval gate, which a dispatched role cannot do

reviewer.reason: it targets a diff, PR, branch or path and scales finding volume by effort level, and can post inline comments or apply fixes

review-lens.reason: it runs its own perspectives internally, so a separate lens role has nothing left to fan out

worktrees.reason: the harness tracks the worktree for the session and cleans it up, so provenance and teardown are not yours to manage here

visual-verification.reason: both build and drive the real app, which is the render evidence this skill exists to demand

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.effortAbsentNote: agents are `model: inherit` and there is no reasoning-effort control, so a tier means its model alone — pick the tier's model in the UI before a batch of same-tier work

opencode.title: OpenCode
opencode.effortAbsentNote: each registered agent always runs its pinned model at the provider's default effort, so no role downscales or upscales per dispatch

claude.note: spawn the named native agent; its generated frontmatter pins both model and effort

cursor.note: plugin agent from the generated Cursor agents directory

opencode.note: registered agent from `agents.json`, spawned via the task tool

claude.note: both, fixed in the agent's own generated frontmatter — a dispatcher does not choose them per call

codex.note: both, chosen per spawn: pass `model` and `reasoning_effort` explicitly; a user or `AGENTS.md` override still wins

cursor.note: neither — agents inherit the model selected in the UI, so a tier is a recommendation here and nothing more

opencode.note: model only, fixed per registered agent; effort is not settable at all

claude.note: native edit denial — the tool allowlist omits Write and Edit; Bash stays shell-capable, so this is not a hard sandbox

codex.note: prompt only — a convention, never a guarantee; never route work here that depends on it

opencode.note: native edit denial — generated `permission.edit: deny`, refused by OpenCode itself; Bash stays shell-capable, so this is not a hard sandbox

claude.note: `EnterWorktree` / `ExitWorktree`, session-tracked and auto-cleaned; pair every Enter with an Exit

codex.note: no native tool — raw `git worktree` at `.claude/worktrees/<name>`

cursor.note: no native tool — raw `git worktree` at `.claude/worktrees/<name>`

opencode.note: no native tool — raw `git worktree` at `.claude/worktrees/<name>`

codex.note: none — fan out by hand and keep the ledger in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py`

cursor.note: none — fan out by hand and keep the ledger in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py`

opencode.note: no runner — `cost-tiered-fix.js` ships in the package but nothing here executes it; fan out by hand and keep the ledger in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py`

claude.note: `TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate` — the harness owns the list and it survives compaction, so do not hand-roll a ledger here

codex.note: no task tool — record progress in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` after every dispatch resolves

cursor.note: no task tool — record progress in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` after every dispatch resolves

opencode.note: no task tool — record progress in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` after every dispatch resolves

claude.note: `SendMessage` to the same agent, which keeps the context it already built

codex.note: `followup_task` to the same live agent; it retains the context it already built

cursor.note: none established — re-dispatch cold with the context restated

opencode.note: none established — re-dispatch cold with the context restated

codex.note: Plan mode `request_user_input` — structured multiple choice; outside Plan mode ask in plain text and default to changing nothing

cursor.note: none established — ask in plain text and default to changing nothing

opencode.note: native `question` tool — multi-choice, single or multi-select

claude.note: the Browser pane (start or attach a preview, then screenshot), an attached Chrome, or the iOS Simulator control tool; some arrive only after a tool search, so an empty tool list is not proof of absence

codex.note: the bundled browser plugin, else computer-use, else Playwright driven from the shell

cursor.note: Browser Preview against a running dev server, else a registered Playwright server

opencode.note: no built-in renderer — a registered Playwright server, or the Playwright CLI, and only where the project already depends on it
`leo-<name>` — OpenCode has no skill namespace, so the adapter registers a renamed copy; read every `leo:<x>` here as `leo-<x>`

reasons.attach-pr: its entire product is a side effect in Claude Code Desktop's PR-card detector, which no other harness has — the same commands would run here, succeed, and produce nothing observable
